H5329: properly, to glitter from afar, i.e. to be eminent (as a superintendent, especially of the Temple services and its music); to be permanent
H4192: 'To die for the son', probably the title of a popular song
H4210: properly, instrumental music; by implication, a poem set to notes
H1732: David, the youngest son of Jesse
H3034: physically, to throw (a stone, an arrow) at or away; especially to revere or worship (with extended hands); intensively, to bemoan (by wringing the hands)
H3068: Jehovah, Jewish national name of God
H3605: properly, the whole; hence, all, any or every (in the singular only, but often in a plural sense)
H3820: the heart; also used (figuratively) very widely for the feelings, the will and even the intellect; likewise for the centre of anything
H5608: properly, to score with a mark as a tally or record, i.e. (by implication) to inscribe, and also to enumerate; intensively, to recount, i.e. celebrate
H6381: properly, perhaps to separate, i.e. distinguish (literally or figuratively); by implication, to be (causatively, make) great, difficult, wonderful
H8055: probably to brighten up, i.e. (figuratively) be (causatively, make) blithe or gleesome
H5970: to jump for joy, i.e. exult
H2167: play upon it; to make music, accompanied by the voice; hence to celebrate in song and music
H8034: an appellation, as amark or memorial of individuality; by implication honor, authority, character
H5945: an elevation, i.e. (adj.) lofty (compar.); as title, the Supreme
H7725: to turn back (hence, away) transitively or intransitively, literally or figuratively (not necessarily with the idea of return to the starting point); generally to retreat; often adverbial, again
H268: the hinder part; hence (adverb) behind, backward; also (as facing north) the West
H3782: to totter or waver (through weakness of the legs, especially the ankle); by implication, to falter, stumble, faint or fall
H6: properly, to wander away, i.e. lose oneself; by implication to perish (causative, destroy)
H6440: the face (as the part that turns); used in a great variety of applications (literally and figuratively); also (with prepositional prefix) as a preposition (before, etc.)
H3588: (by implication) very widely used as a relative conjunction or adverb (as below); often largely modified by other particles annexed
H6213: to do or make, in the broadest sense and widest application
H4941: properly, a verdict (favorable or unfavorable) pronounced judicially, especially a sentence or formal decree (human or (participant's) divine law, individual or collective), including the act, the place, the suit, the crime, and the penalty; abstractly, justice, including a participant's right or privilege (statutory or customary), or even a style
H1779: judgement (the suit, justice, sentence or tribunal); by implication also strife
H3427: properly, to sit down (specifically as judge. in ambush, in quiet); by implication, to dwell, to remain; causatively, to settle, to marry
H3678: properly, covered, i.e. a throne (as canopied)
H8199: to judge, i.e. pronounce sentence (for or against); by implication, to vindicate or punish; by extenssion, to govern; passively, to litigate (literally or figuratively)
H6664: the right (natural, moral or legal); also (abstractly) equity or (figuratively) prosperity
H1471: a foreign nation; hence, a Gentile; also (figuratively) a troop of animals, or a flight of locusts
H7563: morally wrong; concretely, an (actively) bad person
H4229: properly, to stroke or rub; by implication, to erase; also to smooth (as if with oil), i.e. grease or make fat; also to touch, i.e. reach to
H5769: properly, concealed, i.e. the vanishing point; generally, time out of mind (past or future), i.e. (practically) eternity; frequentatively, adverbial (especially with prepositional prefix) always
H5703: properly, a (peremptory) terminus, i.e. (by implication) duration, in the sense of advance or perpetuity (substantially as a noun, either with or without a preposition)
H8552: to complete, in a good or a bad sense, literal, or figurative, transitive or intransitive
H2723: properly, drought, i.e. (by implication) a desolation
H5331: properly, a goal, i.e. the bright object at adistance travelled towards; hence (figuratively), splendor, or (subjectively) truthfulness, or (objectively) confidence; but usually (adverbially), continually (i.e. to the most distant point of view)
H5892: a city (a place guarded by waking or a watch) in the widest sense (even of a mere encampment or post)
H2143: a memento, abstractly recollection (rarely if ever); by implication, commemoration
H3559: properly, to be erect (i.e. stand perpendicular); hence (causatively) to set up, in a great variety of applications, whether literal (establish, fix, prepare, apply), or figurative (appoint, render sure, proper or prosperous)
H1931: he (she or it); only expressed when emphatic or without a verb; also (intensively) self, or (especially with the article) the same; sometimes (as demonstrative) this or that; occasionally (instead of copula) as or are
H8398: the earth (as moist and therefore inhabited); by extension, the globe; by implication, its inhabitants; specifically, a particular land, as Babylonia, Palestine
H1777: a straight course, i.e. sail direct
H4339: evenness, i.e. (figuratively) prosperity or concord; also straightness, i.e. (figuratively) rectitude (only in plural with singular sense; often adverbially)
H1961: to exist, i.e. be or become, come to pass (always emphatic, and not a mere copula or auxiliary)
H4869: defence, high fort (tower), refuge, Misgab, a place in Moab
H6256: time, especially (adverb with preposition) now, when, etc.
H6869: tightness (i.e. figuratively, trouble); transitively, a female rival:
H982: figuratively, to trust, be confident or sure
H3045: to know (properly, to ascertain by seeing); used in a great variety of senses, figuratively, literally, euphemistically and inferentially (including observation, care, recognition; and causatively, instruction, designation, punishment, etc.)
H3808: not (the simple or abs. negation); by implication, no; often used with other particles
H5800: to loosen, i.e. relinquish, permit, etc.
H1875: properly, to tread or frequent; usually to follow (for pursuit or search); by implication, to seek or ask; specifically to worship
H6726: Tsijon (as a permanent capital), a mountain of Jerusalem
H5046: properly, to front, i.e. stand boldly out opposite; by implication (causatively), to manifest; figuratively, to announce (always by word of mouth to one present); specifically, to expose, predict, explain, praise
H5971: a people (as a congregated unit); specifically, a tribe (as those of Israel); hence (collectively) troops or attendants; figuratively, a flock
H5949: an exploit (of God), or a performance (of man, often in a bad sense); by implication, an opportunity
H1818: blood (as that which when shed causes death) of man or an animal; by analogy, the juice of the grape; figuratively (especially in the plural) bloodshed (i.e. drops of blood)
H853: properly, self (but generally used to point out more definitely the object of a verb or preposition, even or namely)
H2142: properly, to mark (so as to be recognized), i.e. to remember; by implication, to mention; to be male
H7911: to mislay, i.e. to be oblivious of, from want of memory or attention
H2603: properly, to bend or stoop in kindness to an inferior; to favor, bestow; causatively to implore (i.e. move to favor by petition)
H7200: to see, literally or figuratively (in numerous applications, direct and implied, transitive, intransitive and causative)
H7311: to be high actively, to rise or raise (in various applications, literally or figuratively)
H8179: an opening, i.e. door or gate
H4194: death (natural or violent); concretely, the dead, their place or state (hades); figuratively, pestilence, ruin
H4616: properly, heed, i.e. purpose; used only adverbially, on account of (as a motive or an aim), teleologically, in order that
H1323: a daughter (used in the same wide sense as other terms of relationship, literally and figuratively)
H1523: properly, to spin round (under the influence of any violent emotion), i.e. usually rejoice, or (as cringing) fear
H3444: something saved, i.e. (abstractly) deliverance; hence, aid, victory, prosperity
H7845: a pit (especially as a trap); figuratively, destruction
H3920: to catch (in a net, trap or pit); generally, to capture or occupy; also to choose (by lot); figuratively, to cohere
H7272: a foot (as used in walking); by implication, a step; by euphemistically the pudenda
H3709: the hollow hand or palm (so of the paw of an animal, of the sole, and even of the bowl of a dish or sling, the handle of a bolt, the leaves of a palm-tree); figuratively, power
H5367: to entrap (with a noose), literally or figuratively
H1902: a murmuring sound, i.e. a musical notation (probably similar to the modern affettuoso to indicate solemnity of movement); by implication, a machination
H7585: Hades or the world of the dead (as if a subterranean retreat), including its accessories and inmates
H430: gods in the ordinary sense; but specifically used (in the plural thus, especially with the article) of the supreme God; occasionally applied by way of deference to magistrates; and sometimes as a superlative
H8615: literally a cord (as an attachment); figuratively, expectancy
H6035: depressed (figuratively), in mind (gentle) or circumstances (needy, especially saintly)
H6965: to rise (in various applications, literal, figurative, intensive and causative)
H408: not (the qualified negation, used as a deprecative); once (Job 24:25) as a noun, nothing
H582: a man in general (singly or collectively)
H5921: above, over, upon, or against (yet always in this last relation with a downward aspect) in a great variety of applications
H7896: to place (in a very wide application)
H4172: fear; by implication, a fearful thing or deed
